articles.title: You can now see and edit what Google Gemini remembers about you - Engadget
articles.descEn: Editing the AI’s memory is one way you can shape its responses.
articles.titleEn: You can now see and edit what Google Gemini remembers about you - Engadget
summaryLinesEn: Depending on what you share, Gemini's picture of you can be fairly intimate, which makes the ability to edit the AI's memory all the more important.
The AI isn't able to create any memories unless it can remember and access your inputs, so Keep Activity needs to be on for this to work.

Besides the ability to connect and use other applications and services, a lot of AI assistants' utility comes from their capacity to shape their responses based on what they learn and remember about you.

Besides the ability to connect and use other applications and services, a lot of AI assistants' utility comes from their capacity to shape their responses based on what they learn and remember about you. Google's Personal Intelligence feature allows Gemini to pull in context from Gmail, YouTube, Search and other Google apps, and the AI also builds out its memory based on your preferences and other personal facts that come up in chats . For example, if you share with Gemini that you're lactose intolerant, the bot will avoid recommending milk-based products.

Depending on what you share, Gemini's picture of you can be fairly intimate, which makes the ability to edit the AI's memory all the more important. If you're curious about what Gemini knows or you want to edit what the AI can draw from to personalize its responses, Google is rolling out a way to see and change Gemini's memory directly from the settings menu.

articles.title: How we raised Databricks cluster rate limits by 7.5× | Databricks Blog
articles.descEn: Learn how adaptive concurrency limits helped Databricks raise cluster-creation request-rate limits by 7.5× while protecting long-running workflows.
articles.titleEn: How we raised Databricks cluster rate limits by 7.5× | Databricks Blog
summaryLinesEn: Conservative limits turned away customer requests despite spare capacity, yet kept accepting requests when our services or dependencies, such as cloud providers, slowed down.
Engineers manually lowered limits to shed load during incidents and raised them again after recovery.

In this post, we'll explore why fixed request-rate limits can fall short for these long-running operations, how adaptive concurrency limits help, and what we learned applying them to cluster creation for Databricks classic compute.

articles.title: Sovereign AI on your terms, made with Europe | Google Cloud Blog
articles.descEn: At the Sovereign AI Summit in Brussels, we announced new Sovereign Cloud from Google solutions to give you more control over your AI stack.
articles.titleEn: Sovereign AI on your terms, made with Europe | Google Cloud Blog
summaryLinesEn: Google Cloud Dedicated is designed so that the local partner controls the environment, can block software updates in exceptional circumstances, and can keep operating for up to 12 months in the unlikely scenario that its Dedicated instance connection to Google is severed.
In May 2025, we introduced a portfolio of sovereign cloud offerings for customers to match their desired level of control to each workload.
With Thales, we are extending Google Cloud Dedicated to Germany (currently in preview), to enable a sovereign hyperscale capability across the EU.

articles.title: Pedestal AI raises $4.7 million to agentify the supply chain
articles.descEn: The company uses agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable.
articles.titleEn: Pedestal AI raises $4.7 million to agentify the supply chain
summaryLinesEn: On Tuesday, Pedestal AI emerged from stealth with $4.7 million in seed funding.
The supply chain startup Atomic , launched by a team of Tesla alumni, came out of stealth in 2025 with an emphasis on streamlining inventory.
Pedestal says the funding will be used to expand its product and engineering time, grow the marketing organization, and support additional deployments.

articles.title: Proton's Lumo, a privacy-focused alternative to ChatGPT and Claude, arrives on desktop
articles.descEn: Proton's new Lumo Desktop app for Windows, Mac, and Linux lets users automate tasks across files and connected apps, with granular controls over what its AI can access.
articles.titleEn: Proton's Lumo, a privacy-focused alternative to ChatGPT and Claude, arrives on desktop
summaryLinesEn: The company says it’s investing in its infrastructure, with its first Nvidia B300 cluster built on Open Compute Project (OCP) standards now going live in Switzerland.
Only this week, for instance, Apple announced it was addressing those privacy concerns with tightened security settings for apps that request Full Disk Access, as the AI desktop apps do.

Already, the major model makers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and others, offer desktop tools for working with their AI technologies, but doing so invites increased risk to users’ personal data .

articles.title: The US wants to block China from renting AI power abroad but China already built a parallel supply chain from US AI output
articles.descEn: The US is tightening its chip export controls. Data centers in third countries like Singapore and Malaysia will soon need a US license to buy Nvidia chips, closing the loophole that let Chinese firms rent cloud compute abroad. A Reuters investigation also reveals how China offsets its hardware shortage through industrial-scale distillation of US AI models.
articles.titleEn: The US wants to block China from renting AI power abroad but China already built a parallel supply chain from US AI output
summaryLinesEn: Nvidia's stock fell as much as 2.9 percent after the announcement, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped up to 5.5 percent.
US officials also confronted Chinese regulators in Chengdu as early as July because Washington sees mass distillation as the main reason for China's rapid AI catch-up, according to Reuters.
The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) at the US Commerce Department now wants to shut down that workaround with an interim rule .

articles.title: Apple adds new disk controls to prevent AI agents from running amok - Engadget
articles.descEn: After sounding an alarm about the issue, Apple is taking steps to limit Mac disk access to AI agents.
articles.titleEn: Apple adds new disk controls to prevent AI agents from running amok - Engadget
summaryLinesEn: The issue rose to prominence in September, when Inc. columnist Jason Aten noticed that Meta's Muse Mac app was able to access his messages even though he thought he had denied that permission.

In its latest macOS beta, Apple introduced controls to ensure that users will need to take "very explicit" actions to grant apps like ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini "this extraordinary level of [full disk] access."
As screen grabs from X user @madeby_ldt show, Apple's Full Disk Access setting now requires explicit permissions to be granted from a scary-looking pop-up screen.

summaryLinesEn: Today, he has proprietary munition and missile designs, several government partnerships, and a defense-as-a-service business valued at more than $1 billion.

articles.title: Rogue Agents Hacked His Company. Why Is Clément Delangue So Optimistic About AI?
articles.descEn: The French CEO of Hugging Face, a mega-hub of open-source AI software, says the attack by OpenAI models earlier this year proved one thing: Humanity can’t let AI be controlled by the few.
articles.titleEn: Rogue Agents Hacked His Company. Why Is Clément Delangue So Optimistic About AI?
summaryLinesEn: Clément Delangue, CEO of the open-source AI company Hugging Face , may go down in history as one of the first people ever attacked by a rogue AI agent.
Delangue moved to the US more than a decade ago, “barely speaking English,” and built Hugging Face into a platform that supports tens of millions of AI developers.
Despite championing the democratization of AI, however, Hugging Face was acquired by one of the industry’s biggest players, Nvidia, for $12.93 billion in September.

articles.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with lower API prices and some benchmark gains
articles.descEn: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, two new models that are more capable and cheaper than their predecessors. In the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Astra ranks second behind Claude Fable 5.2, and it is the first released model to reach the High threshold for AI self-improvement on OpenAI's own scale. OpenAI itself classifies that as a risk.
articles.titleEn: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with lower API prices and some benchmark gains
summaryLinesEn: On the internal GDPval-v2 benchmark, which includes consulting, finance, and design tasks, OpenAI says Astra gains 6.2 percentage points over its predecessor while using 22 percent fewer output tokens.
On the coding benchmark FrontierCode 2.0, which checks whether code changes meet the quality bar of real projects, Sol trails Astra by just 0.5 points at one-fifth the cost.

On Agents' Last Exam, a benchmark that tests multi-step professional workflows, GPT-6.2 Astra scores 5.2 points above its predecessor GPT-6 Astra at less than a third of the cost, according to OpenAI.

OpenAI has released two new models: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. They are on par with Anthropic’s best models, but much more affordable.

Astra is designed for demanding specialized work in science, law, and finance, while Sol is geared toward quick, everyday tasks. Both are now available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users. Astra’s API pricing is 20 percent lower than that of its predecessor.

In the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, GPT-6.2 Astra ranks second, just behind Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2, but according to Artificial Analysis, it dominates the Pareto frontier in terms of cost-performance ratio.

articles.title: Google expands access to Gemini Tasks, which can help with calls, purchases
articles.descEn: Gemini's Task mode can help users coordinate calls, log into websites, and even make purchases on the user's behalf.
articles.titleEn: Google expands access to Gemini Tasks, which can help with calls, purchases
summaryLinesEn: Tasks was initially launched to select testers back in May as Gemini Spark, a 24/7 agentic helper, and was expanded to U.S. subscribers of its Google AI Ultra tier.
Users merely flip a toggle within the app from Chat to Tasks, which enables the feature.

Unlike Gemini’s Chat, which merely allows users to talk to Google’s AI assistant for informational purposes, Tasks empowers the app to complete basic secretarial functions, deputizing it as a kind of personal assistant.

sourceContent.description: Gemini's Task mode can help users coordinate calls, log into websites, and even make purchases on the user's behalf.
paragraphs: Tasks was initially launched to select testers back in May as Gemini Spark, a 24/7 agentic helper, and was expanded to U.S. subscribers of its Google AI Ultra tier.
Users merely flip a toggle within the app from Chat to Tasks, which enables the feature.

Unlike Gemini’s Chat, which merely allows users to talk to Google’s AI assistant for informational purposes, Tasks empowers the app to complete basic secretarial functions, deputizing it as a kind of personal assistant.
Google is expanding the rollout of Tasks, a toggle in Gemini that converts the chatbot into a more active helper.

sourceContent.description: Nvidia's interim CEO reaffirmed its open source AI strategy and plans to acquire Hugging Face, despite Jensen Huang's sudden departure.
paragraphs: Kress also spoke about Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face, a platform for open source AI models that the company agreed to acquire for $12.9 billion in September, in what would be the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia’s history.

Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress reaffirmed the company’s commitment to open source AI during Tuesday’s earnings call with analysts — the first since CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation.

“At Nvidia, we are committed to fostering a vibrant open model ecosystem, so every country, company, and industry can build its own intelligence,” Kress said in her opening remarks. She also noted that open models were accelerating AI adoption, citing a 35-fold year-over-year surge in weekly token volume on OpenRouter, including a 3.5-fold increase over the past three months.

articles.descEn: Innovative fitness band, HONOR band 6, offers a holistic range of health and fitness tracking capabilities to empower people to stay mentally and physically fit.
articles.titleEn: HONOR Band 6 Launches with Bigger Display and Premium Health Monitoring Features

articles.title: Built on object storage, served from cache | Databricks Blog
articles.descEn: Object storage gives Lakebase Postgres its foundation: durable, bottomless storage, instant branches and restores, and one copy of data for transactions and analytics (LTAP).
articles.titleEn: Built on object storage, served from cache | Databricks Blog
summaryLinesEn: They come from old branches, restores, or databases waking up after weeks idle, and once that data is cached, the next reads are local again.

The common argument against running Postgres on object storage goes like this: Object storage is built for larger requests at higher latency, and a single read from it can take hundreds of milliseconds Therefore, a Postgres backed by object storage must be a slow Postgres
The rare reads that do reach object storage are one-offs.

articles.title: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents
articles.descEn: NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science, the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance […]
articles.titleEn: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents
summaryLinesEn: Nsight AI Porting Agent: NVIDIA’s new agent ported a routine from the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model to GPUs, Buck said, speeding it up more than 5x using about 150 million tokens.
In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing .
Buck said a simulation on Jülich’s JUPITER supercomputer showed that a technique called magic state cultivation can cut the operations needed for one logical step tenfold.

articles.title: Your users are already on Arm – is your software targeting it?
articles.descEn: Learn how Arm architecture shapes cloud, gaming, and on-device AI workloads—and how to test, optimize, and scale your software for Arm.
articles.titleEn: Your users are already on Arm – is your software targeting it?
summaryLinesEn: With 99% of smartphones running on Arm, around 50% of Arm-based compute shipped to leading hyperscalers, and more than 350 billion Arm-based chips shipped to date, the Arm architecture already powers many of the platforms developers build for every day.
Once running, benchmarking tools such as Arm Performix can help provide insights into hotspots, memory usage, and CPU efficiency to guide optimization.
That means you can continue building through the operating systems, containers, libraries, and cloud services already in your workflow.

articles.title: Arm enables the world’s fastest and most energy-efficient supercomputers
articles.descEn: The November 2026 TOP500 and Green500 rankings showcase the breadth of the Arm high-performance computing (HPC) ecosystem.
articles.titleEn: Arm enables the world’s fastest and most energy-efficient supercomputers
summaryLinesEn: ⚡ The latest milestone in our collaboration highlights the importance of CPU and accelerator co-design in scaling AI We're expanding Arm Flexible Access and Arm Total Access with the new Arm Cortex-M42 processor.

With 5 of the top 10 and 14 of the top 30 most energy-efficient systems incorporating Arm technology, the rankings reflect the growing adoption of Arm across supercomputing and AI platforms designed to deliver more compute within constrained power budgets.

Arm technology across the world’s leading supercomputers From the world’s most powerful supercomputers to the most energy-efficient systems, Arm technology is helping advance HPC through a diverse range of processors and platforms, including Arm-compatible custom processors and Arm Neoverse-based accelerated systems.

summaryLinesEn: Sensor Tower estimates the game's audience on Android phones in the United States is 72% male and 57% under 35, with a typical age of 34 and middle-income purchasing power.

Sensor Tower's, The Attention Heist: GTA VI's Impact on Consumer Engagement report, sizes the launch, measures how past AAA releases affected the console market, and profiles the average GTA VI player on mobile.

articles.title: How ArisGlobal scaled generative AI inference on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: ArisGlobal runs NavaX, its life-sciences AI engine, on Amazon Bedrock. By caching the shared prompt prefix instead of each per-case document, ArisGlobal cut effective input cost by about 50% and overall monthly inference spend by about 40%, while onboarding more tenants without proportional cost growth.
articles.titleEn: How ArisGlobal scaled generative AI inference on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: As enterprise customers added distinct compliance requirements, the shared prompt prefix grew by about 150% over 6 months, while per-case inference costs increased by more than 200%.
When NavaX launched with its first enterprise tenant, the system prompt was lean.
By reversing the order and caching the shared prefix instead, ArisGlobal reduced effective input cost and supported additional tenants without proportional cost growth.
articles.summary:
As enterprise customers added distinct compliance requirements, the shared prompt prefix grew by about 150% over 6 months, while per-case inference costs increased by more than 200%.
When NavaX launched with its first enterprise tenant, the system prompt was lean.
By reversing the order and caching the shared prefix instead, ArisGlobal reduced effective input cost and supported additional tenants without proportional cost growth.

articles.descEn: Learn how Databricks and Google Cloud enable zero-copy data access through catalog federation and advance open business and governance metadata.

articles.title: Responsible AI for agentic AI: A phased roadmap for platform and application teams | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: Enterprises adopting agentic AI at scale need platforms that embed responsible AI from the start. This post gives platform and application teams a three-phase roadmap (governance foundation, pilot deployment, and evaluation and hardening) that maps the AWS Responsible AI Lens pillars to each phase, with guidance on when to revisit each one.
articles.titleEn: Responsible AI for agentic AI: A phased roadmap for platform and application teams | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: Organizations are turning Responsible AI, which includes the pillars of security and privacy, veracity and robustness, fairness, safety, controllability, explainability, transparency, and governance into a growth strategy by addressing its expanding scope early.

We break the journey into three phases and present prioritized responsible AI pillars across a customizable 12-week implementation timeline, allowing the platform team to establish a solid responsible AI foundation while their first use cases take shape.
The application teams classify risks for each planned use case using a risk rubric.

articles.title: Google Wallet is now available on iOS in the U.S.
articles.descEn: Google Wallet is now available on iOS in the U.S. Manage your tickets, boarding passes, and receipts in one secure hub. Get the details.
articles.titleEn: Google Wallet is now available on iOS in the U.S.
summaryLinesEn: Today, we’re bringing Google Wallet to iOS users across the U.S., making it faster to get what you need and easier to organize purchases, tickets, boarding passes, and more in one easy place.

As we look toward the future of shopping, Google Wallet will also be a secure hub for managing agentic purchases across Google, and today’s update expands access to more people, no matter what type of device they use.
By automatically syncing with your Gmail and other Google apps, Google Wallet keeps your package tracking, digital boarding passes, concert tickets, and receipts anywhere easily across your devices.

articles.title: Temporary threads are now available in AI Mode in Search.
articles.descEn: Google AI Mode now offers temporary threads for private searches. Keep your history clean and avoid personalization. Try this new feature today.
articles.titleEn: Temporary threads are now available in AI Mode in Search.
summaryLinesEn: We’re introducing temporary threads in AI Mode, where you can explore and ask questions — whether that’s brainstorming a surprise gift or looking something up you don’t want resurfaced later like in your history or recommendations.
There’s no need to adjust your settings — you can quickly jump into a temporary thread for any query you don't want saved, and switch right back when you're done.
To get started, simply click the temporary threads icon in the upper right corner of AI Mode and start asking your questions.

articles.title: Put Gemini to work for you
articles.descEn: Tasks in Gemini is now free of charge in six countries, with new features starting in the U.S. and deeper Google Workspace integration to get things done on your behalf.
articles.titleEn: Put Gemini to work for you
summaryLinesEn: I recently stared down a nearly empty fridge rushing out the door in the morning, and I texted Gemini with the new RCS integration 2 : “Add lasagna, strawberries, cucumbers, and vanilla ice cream to our Instacart order.”
Because Gemini already knows we drive a 2019 Honda Odyssey and where we live through Personal Intelligence , it found the nearest shops on Google Maps and called both at once 1 .
Last month it saved us real money after we got hit with a surprise $389 electric bill.

articles.title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale
articles.descEn: Claude formally proved security properties in the compiled code of 123 open-source libraries. Along the way, it found bugs that had eluded detection for years.
articles.titleEn: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale
summaryLinesEn: Formal software verification could provide this guarantee, but it has historically required years of expert effort, making it impractical for most real-world projects.

Theorem , our collaborator on this project, is also offering to run the same pipeline for other open-source projects , and is publishing a Claude skill to help developers get started with verifying their own code.
As model capabilities continue to improve, we expect formal verification to become an essential part of secure software development.

articles.title: Meet the AI Assistant for Healthcare — Abridge
articles.descEn: A clinical AI assistant has to know the patient and pass a health system review before the first question. Matt Troup and Janie Lee on why we built the Abridge Assistant.
articles.titleEn: Meet the AI Assistant for Healthcare — Abridge
summaryLinesEn: Most of the standalone tools I’ve used share the same problem, regardless of how much they tout AI.
Abridge led the shift to ambient AI in clinical documentation, centering the patient conversation and cutting the after-hours charting clinicians used to take home .
The tasks pile up right behind them, and each one means more time clicking through the chart before the shift ends.

sourceContent.headline: Meet the AI Assistant for Healthcare — Abridge
sourceContent.description: A clinical AI assistant has to know the patient and pass a health system review before the first question. Matt Troup and Janie Lee on why we built the Abridge Assistant.
paragraphs: Most of the standalone tools I’ve used share the same problem, regardless of how much they tout AI.
Abridge led the shift to ambient AI in clinical documentation, centering the patient conversation and cutting the after-hours charting clinicians used to take home .
The tasks pile up right behind them, and each one means more time clicking through the chart before the shift ends.
The next era of clinical software won’t be clicked through. It’ll be talked to.

Abridge led the shift to ambient AI in clinical documentation, centering the patient conversation and cutting the after-hours charting clinicians used to take home . Yet, the rest of the day is still spent on tabs, clicks, and navigating fields. Clinicians should be able to do what everyone else can now do with consumer chatbots and agents: say what they need and get it.

That’s why we built the Abridge Assistant , the AI assistant for healthcare. The Assistant is built from the same AI research and clinician-led evaluation that brought Abridge’s ambient notes to more than 300 enterprise health systems. Clinicians can ask questions and delegate tasks to the Assistant in their own words. As of our September release, every clinician at every Abridge health system has access to the Assistant , whether or not they use Abridge for documentation.

articles.title: Healthcare Is Presence: Building the Learning Health System — Abridge
articles.descEn: How AI assistants could finally make the Learning Health System real, and allow clinicians to focus on the patient in front of them.
articles.titleEn: Healthcare Is Presence: Building the Learning Health System — Abridge
summaryLinesEn: The work might include entering data into a registry or a clinical trial management system, calling the inpatient pharmacy to get medications ready, navigating to a payer portal to get authorization for a life saving medication, and scheduling follow-up testing and an outpatient visit.

Twenty years ago, the Institute of Medicine introduced the concept of a Learning Health System: a system that continuously improves, so the right information gets to the right care team member at the right moment.
Today, we partner with more than 300 health systems and support more than 140 million encounters every year.

Twenty years ago, the Institute of Medicine introduced the concept of a Learning Health System: a system that continuously improves, so the right information gets to the right care team member at the right moment. A system that uses what it learns from caring for one patient to take better care of the next.
It’s been twenty years. We talk about it every single year. Have we made real progress?

A few years ago, the Kaiser Family Foundation published a piece called “ Death by a Thousand Clicks .” It described emergency medicine clinicians clicking 4,000 times to get through a single shift, and the patient experience suffering because of that split attention. Every clinician knows what that feels like. You’re with a patient, but part of your attention is somewhere else.

sourceContent.headline: Introducing the new Microsoft IQ
sourceContent.description: Discover Microsoft IQ, the enterprise context management platform that unifies business knowledge and data to build trusted AI agents.
paragraphs: Web IQ is now available to every Azure customer , with no waitlist and pricing starting at $1 per 1,000 calls.
A supply chain team can speed up supplier risk and disruption response.

Introducing the new Microsoft IQ: Putting your organization’s intelligence to work in every agent
Customer spotlight: AEMO uses Microsoft IQ to keep Australia’s grid secure

Microsoft believes that AI should enhance your advantage, not erode it. Every organization has access to the same frontier models, and those models improve every few weeks. Today at Microsoft Ignite 2026, we’re announcing the general availability of Azure Cobalt 200-based virtual machines (VMs) . Cobalt 200 VMs deliver up to 50% better performance than Cobalt 100 and are now available in 14 regions, expanding to 23 regions by the end of 2026. Built for cloud-native, data-intensive, and agentic AI workloads, Cobalt 200 VMs will represent a significant share of new Azure Compute capacity beginning in 2027.

Introducing Azure Catalyst agentic modernization and new AI infrastructure innovations

As AI continues to reshape how every business builds, operates, and competes, it is rapidly emerging as the defining workload in the cloud. This new class of agents, more demanding, complex, and dynamic than anything before them, is rewriting the rules of cloud infrastructure. Reasoning across multi-agent systems, drawing on rich context, acting in real time, and running continuously, they ask more of every layer of the platform beneath them. This week, we’re introducing innovations across Microsoft Azure that set a new standard for how the cloud powers AI: expanded AI core capabilities in Azure to build what’s next, and Azure Catalyst, an intelligent agent-led solution to modernize the apps, data, and infrastructure that already run the business.

For years, we have been reengineering every layer of Azure for the unique demands of AI and proving it on the world’s most advanced AI workloads, from leading frontier models to our own GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft 365. That work has forged Azure into a single, co-engineered system, with models, silicon, and cloud infrastructure tuned as one and value compounding at every layer. This week, we take that even further.

articles.title: Microsoft and Oracle turn data into insights and actions
articles.descEn: Learn how Oracle and Microsoft are helping customers modernize to improve application performance and unlock more value from enterprise data.
articles.titleEn: Microsoft and Oracle turn data into insights and actions
summaryLinesEn: Our new integrations let AI agents reason across Oracle’s business-critical data—from finance and supply chain to HR and customer operations—and the work context Microsoft Work IQ understands across meetings, email, documents, and Teams.

Together, Microsoft and Oracle are bringing intelligence to the workflows that run the business: giving analysts, planners and controllers the power to understand margin changes, analyze shifts in demand, resolve reconciliation issues, and act on supply chain disruptions.

“With Cobalt 200, we’re building on our collaboration with Arm to deliver the performance and efficiency our customers need as cloud and AI workloads evolve,” said Reynold D’Sa, CVP Silicon, Cloud Hardware, and Infrastructure Engineering, Microsoft.

At Microsoft Ignite 2026, Microsoft announced the general availability of Azure Cobalt 200 virtual machines (VMs), bringing its latest Arm-based custom CPU to customers running demanding cloud and agentic AI workloads.

articles.descEn: Arm-powered Microsoft Azure Cobalt 200 virtual machines (VMs) deliver performance improvements across cloud-native and agentic AI workloads.
articles.titleEn: How Arm Neoverse CSS-based Microsoft Cobalt 200 virtual machines accelerate cloud and agentic AI performance
summaryLinesEn: With configurations scaling up to 128 vCPUs and 512 GiB of memory, Cobalt 200 provides additional flexibility for enterprises deploying demanding cloud applications.
Recent engineering work introduced Arm NEON and dot-product optimizations for 4-bit quantized vector operations, accelerating an important computational component of vector search.
Microsoft DiskANN delivers 1.45x higher geometric-mean vector-search QPS on Cobalt 200 versus Cobalt 100.

articles.titleEn: Branch, sync, serve: What our Lakebase Hackathon taught us about building on Lakebase | Databricks Blog
summaryLinesEn: The two tracks line up with two ways teams use Lakebase: building applications on it with database branching, and connecting it to the lakehouse to serve data and ML features in real time.
A new branch is created instantly using copy-on-write storage, so you only pay for the data that changes, and creating one has no performance impact on production.
Teams work together for about a week and submit a project, and the strongest solutions earn prizes.

sourceContent.description: Amazon SageMaker AI now offers AI data preparation capabilities for building high-quality training and evaluation data. Generate synthetic examples, assess and improve datasets, auto-label at scale, and bring in expert review through Python SDK APIs and an agent skill, all from your own notebook or IDE.
paragraphs: Quality problems such as duplicates, label noise, and answer leakage go unnoticed until a training run disappoints, and every training technique expects data in its own format.
You choose the preparation steps your project needs and how they fit into your model customization and evaluation processes.
One pass through the preparation workflow looks like this: Define the requirements: Supply the product guide as context and describe the questions and reference answers you need.

Teams that ship generative AI to production know that a model is only as good as its data. That is why preparing high-quality training and evaluation data comes first. Fine-tuning an open-weight model, running reinforcement learning, or building an evaluation suite all depend on data that is accurate, well-labeled, and representative of your task. For narrow, well-defined tasks, a smaller model customized on clean, task-specific data can often match or exceed the accuracy of a larger general-purpose model prompted into shape, at a lower cost per inference.

In practice, though, preparing that data is often the slowest part of the project. Labeled examples are scarce or expensive, and privacy rules limit what you can use. Quality problems such as duplicates, label noise, and answer leakage go unnoticed until a training run disappoints, and every training technique expects data in its own format. As a result, data scientists spend weeks wrangling data instead of building models.

Today, we’re expanding Amazon SageMaker AI with new AI data preparation capabilities for model development workflows. You can generate synthetic examples, assess and improve existing datasets, and bring expert feedback into the process through Python SDK APIs and the AWS AI-ML agent skill. You work in your notebook or IDE, with specifications and code that you can inspect and change.

articles.title: Secure OAuth patterns for Snowflake Cortex AI through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: When an AI agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore calls Snowflake Cortex AI over MCP, how does it authenticate? This post walks through three OAuth patterns we tested on AgentCore Identity: Snowflake OAuth, three-legged OAuth with a corporate IdP, and two-legged OAuth, so you can match your organization's identity, audit, and compliance needs.
articles.titleEn: Secure OAuth patterns for Snowflake Cortex AI through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: The reference implementation sets it to 86400 seconds (1 day), and Snowflake allows up to 90 days.

When an AI agent running on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model) needs to call the Snowflake-managed MCP server (which exposes Snowflake Cortex Agents as one of its tool types) through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the first question enterprises must answer is: how does the agent authenticate?

Figure 1: Solution overview: the reference agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, combining Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Snowflake Cortex AI through the Snowflake-managed MCP server, and the authorization server that differs across the three OAuth patterns The following sections examine each pattern in detail: the authentication flow, configuration steps, and trade-offs to help you select the right approach for your use case.

sourceContent.description: When an AI agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore calls Snowflake Cortex AI over MCP, how does it authenticate? This post walks through three OAuth patterns we tested on AgentCore Identity: Snowflake OAuth, three-legged OAuth with a corporate IdP, and two-legged OAuth, so you can match your organization's identity, audit, and compliance needs.
paragraphs: The reference implementation sets it to 86400 seconds (1 day), and Snowflake allows up to 90 days.

When an AI agent running on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model) needs to call the Snowflake-managed MCP server (which exposes Snowflake Cortex Agents as one of its tool types) through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the first question enterprises must answer is: how does the agent authenticate?

Figure 1: Solution overview: the reference agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, combining Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Snowflake Cortex AI through the Snowflake-managed MCP server, and the authorization server that differs across the three OAuth patterns The following sections examine each pattern in detail: the authentication flow, configuration steps, and trade-offs to help you select the right approach for your use case.

Enterprises today need a clear way to extend their authentication and authorization controls into the agentic layer, often requiring either broad service account permissions or custom-built auth integrations that add operational overhead. When an AI agent running on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model) needs to call the Snowflake-managed MCP server (which exposes Snowflake Cortex Agents as one of its tool types) through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the first question enterprises must answer is: how does the agent authenticate? In this post, we walk through three Open Authorization (OAuth) configurations we tested on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Snowflake OAuth (per-user, no external Identity Provider, or IdP), three-legged OAuth with a third-party Identity Provider (corporate single sign-on, or SSO), and two-legged OAuth with a third-party Identity Provider (shared service user). Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity also supports an on-behalf-of (OBO) grant (TOKEN_EXCHANGE) that delivers per-user identity for unattended workloads without a consent prompt. We focus on the three configurations we tested end-to-end, flagging where OBO fits as we go. By the end, you will be able to identify which pattern suits your enterprise scenario.

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, connects AI agents to external tool providers through MCP server targets. It targets the Snowflake-managed MCP server, which surfaces Cortex Search and Cortex Analyst as MCP tools that an MCP-aware client can discover and invoke. Rather than acting as a wrapper, the Gateway aggregates the capabilities of its configured targets into a single unified catalog, which it presents to the agent as one tools/list response.

The core focus of this post is the outbound authentication for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway: how it obtains and presents OAuth tokens to the Snowflake-managed MCP server. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity acts as the credential broker: the Gateway obtains a workload token by calling GetWorkloadAccessTokenForJWT (because the Gateway uses JSON Web Token (JWT) inbound authentication), then calls GetResourceOauth2Token against the configured provider. AgentCore Identity owns the token vault, the token refresh, and the user-to-token binding, and it fetches, caches, and refreshes tokens automatically.

sourceContent.headline: Govern and discover records with common metadata in AWS Agent Registry | Amazon Web Services
sourceContent.description: Custom metadata schemas in AWS Agent Registry let an administrator define typed, validated fields that every agent, MCP server, and skill must carry. This post follows an MCP record from schema definition through registration, enrichment, approval, and discovery, so teams govern and find resources with one shared set of facts.
paragraphs: When publishers create or submit records, they supply values for the fields specified in the applicable schema, and AWS Agent Registry validates those values against the schema set by the admin.
Because teams can describe the AWS Agent Registry records with the same fields and values, the registry can support and scale governance and compliance.
When a record is created or updated, the registry validates the custom metadata against the schema set up by the admin.

As organizations build more agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and skills, they need a consistent way to describe, govern, and find them. AWS Agent Registry provides a catalog for registering, approving, and discovering these resources and custom records. Each record carries a name, a description, a protocol descriptor, and an approval status. However, every organization has attributes and facts that it wants to track, and some are unique to that organization, such as its business units, resource owners, risk classifications, and development environments. Organizations want one common definition for each of these attributes, and they want every agent, MCP server, and skill in the registry to carry these facts. Until now, organizations had no way to define these facts in AWS Agent Registry and store them on each record.

Custom metadata schemas are now available in AWS Agent Registry. A custom metadata schema is a set of organization-defined key-value pairs that records in an AWS Agent Registry carry. An administrator defines the schema and applies it to the registry, and all records within the registry must then adhere to the schema. When publishers create or submit records, they supply values for the fields specified in the applicable schema, and AWS Agent Registry validates those values against the schema set by the admin. Approvers can rely on the validated values when reviewing a record, and consumers and agents can use them to discover and filter records. Administrators, publishers, security and governance teams, approvers, consumers, and agents all work from a shared set of facts to govern, discover, and understand the resources in their agentic fleet.

In this post, we follow the AnyCompany organization publishing an MCP server with custom schema definition, enriching that record, and making it available for discovery by humans or agents. We use an MCP server as the example, but the same steps apply to other record types.

paragraphs: Compared with random routing, and with long prompts under load, KV-aware routing reduced p50 time to first token (TTFT) by up to 97 percent and increased throughput by up to 234 percent.
In part 1 of this series , we introduced prefix-aware routing for Amazon SageMaker AI, which sends requests that start the same way to the same instance.

Today, Amazon SageMaker AI introduces KV cache-aware routing (KV-aware routing), a new routing strategy for real-time endpoints. It uses the cache state that the model container reports. It sends each request to an instance that already holds a long cached match for its prompt and isn’t too busy. It’s for teams that serve large language models (LLMs) with multi-turn conversations, long shared prompts, or heavy load. You turn it on in two places: add one environment variable to your model so the container reports its cache contents, and set RoutingStrategy to KV_AWARE in the endpoint configuration. Your clients call the endpoint with the same APIs as before.

Here’s the problem it solves: LLM applications such as chat assistants, Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and agents with long system prompts send many requests that start with the same text. A model keeps the work it did on a prompt in GPU memory, the KV cache, and skips that work when the same start reaches the same instance again. In part 1 of this series , we introduced prefix-aware routing for Amazon SageMaker AI, which sends requests that start the same way to the same instance. Prefix-aware routing infers where a prefix is cached from the request alone, so it can’t tell when an instance has evicted that cache.

Prefix-aware routing picks an instance from the request alone. It hashes the start of the request, up to the PrefixLength you configure (bytes of the InvokeEndpoint payload, or characters of the message text for the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API), and sends requests that start the same way to the same instance. It never sees what an instance actually has cached. This works well when every request starts with the same shared text, and less well in two cases:

The biggest cost lever in a generative AI system is whether you call a model at all. We often see teams route every task through a large language model (LLM), including input validation, formatting, and routing. Each call is cheap in isolation, but at production scale these small costs become one of the largest line items in the architecture. Wherever a deterministic rule can do the job, skipping the model saves money, cuts latency, and removes a source of non-determinism. In this post, you learn how to decide whether each step in a workflow needs a model at all. You can then map each option to AWS: deterministic code, a constrained decision call, or a right-sized model on Amazon Bedrock .

The pattern usually starts in a prototype. A model call works for one step, so it becomes the default for the next. Those steps include validating input, reformatting a request body, and picking a route. At prototype volume, nobody notices the cost.
At production volume, unneeded model calls cost you in three ways:

In our latest installment of the Ask a Scientist series, a Google DeepMind research scientist explains the potential behind our AlphaGenome and AlphaGenome Atlas tools.

Your genome is your body’s instruction manual: the blueprint that informs how your body functions. It contains 3 billion base pairs of DNA. Because this DNA is responsible in part for switching genes on and off, it could be the difference between developing a disease and avoiding one. Determining which DNA changes cause diseases (and other outcomes) is like finding a needle in a haystack.

Decoding the DNA sequence is the goal behind AlphaGenome , a model from Google DeepMind. AlphaGenome can take a partial DNA sequence of 1 million base pairs in length, and make thousands of predictions. By comparing these predictions for DNA changes, scientists can find that needle faster.

Over multi-turn conversations, this pressure compounds, driving up costs and degrading response quality.

As enterprises build production agents with dozens of tools and large structured inputs, token consumption and latency become the primary blockers to a good user experience. When these agents process large JSON data, every additional tool invocation injects the full payload into the large language model (LLM) context window, causing token usage and response latency to spike. Over multi-turn conversations, this pressure compounds, driving up costs and degrading response quality. Effectively managing context-window pressure in agentic systems is key to reliability and responsiveness at scale. In this post, we share three composable strategies we used to build a production agent for Flightscape that handles 20 MB+ JSON payloads. You can apply them to reduce token costs, lower latency, and maintain full reasoning capability across extended sessions. Together, these optimizations reduced token consumption by up to 71% and cut average latency by up to 80% across our benchmark runs on a representative 23 MB payload.

Flightscape is an airline operations platform that helps airlines plan and manage their crews, flights, and operations. As part of Flightscape’s crew management capabilities, we built a Training Schedule Optimization agent that verifies crew training schedule assignments against business rules. With 40+ tools and JSON inputs in megabytes, this agent could answer complex queries across crew assignments, scheduling, and resource allocation. Although the agent delivered the required functionality, average request latencies exceeded 15 seconds across most calls. Every tool call injected its full payload into the model context, inflating token counts and costs. On larger datasets, the context window filled up before the agent could finish reasoning. The following diagram (Figure 1) details the agentic architecture and data flow:

In Figure 1, the Optimizer receives a Request JSON and produces a Response JSON, which is then validated by a Business Rules Validator to generate a Validation Report JSON. All three JSON documents are ingested by an AI Agent that provides a conversational interface for users to query optimization results, understand validation errors, and explore scheduling assignments. The agent is built with LangGraph , an open source framework by LangChain, and runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore , a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails can be applied to validate and filter the agent’s conversational responses, helping facilitate responsible AI practices in production deployments. We defined a custom agent state that holds the data needed by our tools: optimization request JSON, optimization response JSON, and validation report JSON. We also added basic statistics and cache data to state for rich queries. The agent uses an Amazon Bedrock model for reasoning and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, to persist chat interactions across turns, and each turn follows this flow (Figure 2):

Serving large language models (LLMs) efficiently requires sufficient GPU memory and careful coordination of prompt processing and token generation. GLM-5.3’s FP8 weights, for example, exceed the 640 GB of GPU memory on a single ml.p5.48xlarge instance, before accounting for KV cache and runtime overhead. Long prompts can also slow token generation when both share the same GPUs.

Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference now supports NVIDIA Dynamo , combining Dynamo’s distributed inference capabilities with the infrastructure management of HyperPod to address these challenges. Dynamo is an open source distributed inference framework that supports multi-node deployment, disaggregated prefill and decode, and KV-aware routing with engines such as vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM. HyperPod supports these deployments with high-performance Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking, coordinated GPU scheduling, and node health monitoring and recovery. In this post, we illustrate multi-node and disaggregated serving through a deployment example, share benchmark results, and outline best practices for optimizing inference on HyperPod.

articles.titleEn: Lam Research Corporation (LRCX): Long-Term Competitive Advantage Outweighs AI Buildout Volatility
summaryLinesEn: On November 16, 2026, Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX) closed at $210.83 per share with a market capitalization of $263.36 billion.

This, despite the company reporting strong quarterly results underlined by accelerating revenue and operating income growth to 30% and 41%, year on-year, respectively, guiding for further acceleration into next quarter with revenue growth of over 50%.

We remain shareholders and believe that Lam is well positioned to benefit from several robust secular tailwinds – from the AI buildout which is driving broad demand for semiconductors, to the increasing complexity and verticalization of chips over time, which raises the number of etch and deposition steps, increasing the demand for Lam's tools."

paragraphs: Less than two years later, OpenAI announced it was shutting down Sora.
The early coverage introduced Kling as Sora’s rival from China.
By then, the company that had needed an American reference point to introduce itself was being priced on the business it had built.
Editor’s note: This article is republished from Jumpstart , a TechNode Group publication.

In the summer of 2024, while most people were still waiting to try OpenAI’s Sora, a rival turned up across the Pacific. It came from Kuaishou, a Chinese short-video company better known at home than abroad. The early coverage introduced Kling as Sora’s rival from China. There was one immediate reason to pay attention. You could already try it.

That was the summer Kling got famous as somebody else’s rival. Less than two years later, OpenAI announced it was shutting down Sora. By October, Kling had reportedly picked banks for a Hong Kong IPO that could raise at least US$1 billion, according to Bloomberg. By then, the company that had needed an American reference point to introduce itself was being priced on the business it had built.

articles.descEn: LanceDB raises $57.5M to accelerate AI model training with multimodal data platform - SiliconANGLE
articles.titleEn: LanceDB raises $57.5M to accelerate AI model training with multimodal data platform - SiliconANGLE
summaryLinesEn: The sheer amount of data included in lidar 3D clouds, images, video, audio and more can take up, on average, 10 to 20 petabytes of data in a single table for many large training workflows, with some becoming even larger – potentially approaching 80 to 100 petabytes.
Notable customers include Runway AI Inc., which adopted LanceDB’s enterprise platform as its AI training needs expanded.

LanceDB is tackling this problem by providing a unified multimodal data lakehouse, giving researchers, enterprise outfits and AI agents a unified way to access, find, prepare and train on that data without spending weeks managing the underlying infrastructure.

articles.title: Jordan Belfort’s new AI voice startup, Tone, wants to sell like the 'Wolf of Wall Street'
articles.descEn: Belfort claims his AI sales voice can already close deals almost as well as the best human salespeople, and he thinks it will catch up in a year.
articles.titleEn: Jordan Belfort’s new AI voice startup, Tone, wants to sell like the 'Wolf of Wall Street'
summaryLinesEn: You might think someone who spent 22 months in prison and was ordered to pay $110.4 million in restitution to 1,513 victims wouldn’t get another shake.

It’s easy to argue the market is already saturated with AI voice startups and technologies, and Tone comes with added risk: Belfort’s co-founder in the business is longtime investor Shervin Pishevar, who has a controversial past of his own.

articles.title: Moonshot AI pivots Kimi models from coding to science as benchmark gains flatten
articles.descEn: Moonshot AI is done chasing coding benchmarks, it says. The Beijing startup is pivoting its Kimi language models toward biology, chemistry, and pharma research, arguing that science demands smarter AI than law, finance, or code.
articles.titleEn: Moonshot AI pivots Kimi models from coding to science as benchmark gains flatten
summaryLinesEn: A June Citi survey of 50 US research leaders found 72 percent already using AI broadly, but only 24 percent expect it to noticeably improve drug development success rates.
Because Moonshot AI sees diminishing returns in coding, the Beijing startup is redirecting its Kimi language models toward biology, chemistry, and pharma research.
In one test, the AI analyzed gene data from 3,696 mouse pancreatic cells and flagged 100 candidate genes in 90 minutes instead of an estimated four hours of human work.

articles.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra tackles the Standard Model's toughest math problem on a lattice
articles.descEn: OpenAI physicist Nathaniel Craig used GPT-6 Astra to tackle a problem that had stumped particle physicists for over 25 years. The AI model took Craig's strategy for defining the full Standard Model on a computational lattice and turned it into a working proof. Craig says a lot of work remains before realistic simulations are possible.
articles.titleEn: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra tackles the Standard Model's toughest math problem on a lattice
summaryLinesEn: Special lattice particles called overlap fermions can filter them out, but for over 25 years, nobody could set their phase correctly.
Ad Craig had a strategy to fix the phase by comparing progressively finer lattices, but couldn't prove it worked in all the cases it needed to cover.
OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra helped produce a proof that could solve a 50-year-old problem in particle physics.

articles.title: Building AI that can work across the enterprise
articles.descEn: For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate. Organizations moving from isolated pilots toward AI agents and autonomous workflows are confronting a deeper challenge: rethinking how data, business processes, governance,…
articles.titleEn: Building AI that can work across the enterprise
summaryLinesEn: The path forward is really to treat AI not just as a project, but more holistically, as an enterprise platform, one that really consistently connects an unified data layer with the process context of the applications, and then embed AI capabilities governed across the entire life cycle.
For Thorsten Leiduck, SVP and global head of SAP Business AI Platform Ecosystem, that shift begins with treating AI as an enterprise platform rather than a collection of disconnected projects.

But, at a time when applications are being scaled up from that initial phase of experimentation, we're still seeing senior leaders grapple with questions around AI's value, risk, and the complexity it adds.

articles.title: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
articles.descEn: In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t. No rule had told the agents to do…
articles.titleEn: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
summaryLinesEn: That is very different from asking whether a model scored 94% on a benchmark.

One contributor argues that having a human in the loop is an insufficient solution because humans are fundamentally unable to understand AI systems’ intentions and advocates instead for interdisciplinary research and collaboration between academia, government, and the tech industry.
Therefore, the goal must be bounded, observable, and controllable AI.

articles.title: Hugging Face and OpenRouter join forces to make open-weight models easy to run
articles.descEn: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
articles.titleEn: Hugging Face and OpenRouter join forces to make open-weight models easy to run
summaryLinesEn: This week, the most used model on OpenRouter is an open-weight one, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, with 59.2 trillion tokens ( rankings ).
Open-weight models cost about four times less on average: $0.28 per million input tokens and $1.62 per million output tokens, against $1.27 and $6.36 for closed models.
On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index , Kimi K3.1 Pro, the best open-weight model, scores 46 against 65 for Claude Fable 5.2, at about a seventh of the cost per task ($3.68 against $26.54).

articles.title: Non-custodial wallets' growing prevalence calls for investor protection
articles.titleEn: Non-custodial wallets' growing prevalence calls for investor protection
summaryLinesEn: However, with NCWs likely to gain prevalence as their UIs continue to get userfriendlier, the current absence of investor protection for NCW users is a concern.
Trading cryptoassets using a non-custodial (aka self-custody) wallet is currently outside the purview of Japan’s crypto regulations.
Japan would be well advised to look more deeply into providing such protection instead of leaving NCW users to fend for themselves.

Japan would be well advised to look more deeply into providing such protection instead of leaving NCW users to fend for themselves.

articles.title: Intent governance in the agentic AI age
articles.titleEn: Intent governance in the agentic AI age
summaryLinesEn: The intent data generated through AI agent interactions will become a valuable strategic asset.
AI agents are set to go live in the financial sector but existing authentication, authorization and auditing functions are not designed for autonomous AI.
As a result, financial institutions may face risks arising from misalignment between a human user's intended objectives and an AI agent's actions.

articles.title: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities
articles.descEn: Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents.
articles.titleEn: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities
summaryLinesEn: AI Day Seoul sessions will soon be available on NVIDIA On-Demand .

The Agentic AI 10x Bootcamp Community Day brought together Pseudo Lab, Python Korea, PyTorchKR, HAERAE, Hugging Face KREW, Graph User Group, Womxn Who Code Korea, Dnol (Datayanolja) and other developer communities.

At the plenary sessions, Deepu Talla, vice president of robotics and edge AI at NVIDIA, said Korea is “punching above its weight,” with Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group — as well as startups like Real World and Luda Robotics — using NVIDIA platforms to bring general-purpose robotics into the real world.

articles.title: Listening to teens on online safety
articles.descEn: Will Gardner, CEO of Childnet, explains how teenagers are embracing AI creatively and responsibly, emphasising the vital role of listening to young voices when navigating online safety.
articles.titleEn: Listening to teens on online safety
summaryLinesEn: This mass adoption of this technology is very much in line with our own research released in February for Safer Internet Day 2026 , which found that nearly all young people aged 8 to 17 (97%) use AI tools, with 58% saying that AI makes their lives better.
Both pieces of work show that young people are aware of the risks or challenges which come with spending time online, and of the impact of an overreliance on AI and other emerging technologies.
Childnet has worked towards making the internet a great and safe place for over 30 years; however, it feels like concerns around online safety have never been higher.

articles.title: Helping teens navigate online news and information
articles.descEn: Rachel Huggins, CEO of Internet Matters, explains how UK teens navigate AI and online news, highlighting the need for media literacy support from educators, platforms, and parents.
articles.titleEn: Helping teens navigate online news and information
summaryLinesEn: This is echoed in Internet Matters’ own research, which found that the growth of this content is leaving children feeling less trusting of the news they encounter in their feeds and more concerned about their ability to distinguish between what is true and false online.
Parents will also continue to be children’s main source of information about online safety, and who they turn to when they need support.

Encouragingly, Google’s research found that many teenagers are already using strategies to verify online information, including cross-checking sources (49%), checking the credibility of websites and authors (48%) and speaking to parents and trusted adults about the content they have seen online (45%).

articles.title: What teenagers really think about online safety and AI
articles.descEn: CEO of ParentZone, Vicki Shotbolt, explains how UK teens are digitally curious and alert to online risks, relying on parent support and using AI creatively to learn.
articles.titleEn: What teenagers really think about online safety and AI
summaryLinesEn: Of the 6,000 UK teenagers surveyed, 77% said they always or often stop to consider whether what they find online can be trusted.

That learning takes place with the help, guidance, and involvement of parents and teachers Eighty-one percent of teens say they would ask a parent for help with misinformation, scams or cyberbullying, and that barely drops as they get older (83% of 13 to 15s, 79% of 16 to 18s).
The report tells us that 52% of 16 to 18 year olds always check what they find, compared with 33% of 13 to 15 year olds.

The report tells us that 52% of 16 to 18 year olds always check what they find, compared with 33% of 13 to 15 year olds

articles.title: Frightfully Competitive Halloween for Candy on Retail Media
articles.descEn: This Halloween, Retail media impressions for candy hit record highs, fueled by an earlier start and a wider field of challengers. Here's how brands fought.
articles.titleEn: Frightfully Competitive Halloween for Candy on Retail Media
summaryLinesEn: Candy Advertisers Got an Early Start on a Record Halloween Retail media impressions in the candy category reached a record 750M in October 2026, outpacing last year’s previous high by +9% YoY.
After prioritizing Instacart in 2025, Reese’s shifted their retail media focus toward Walmart (40M) and Walgreens (28M) in 2026, which together accounted for two-thirds of their October impressions.
This Halloween, the candy competition got a little scarier for the category’s leaders.

articles.title: Innovation at the Speed of Trust: Continuous Improvement in Clinical AI — Abridge
articles.descEn: Discover how Abridge builds specialty-specific clinical AI models—using multi-layered validation to ensure safe, seamless updates.
articles.titleEn: Innovation at the Speed of Trust: Continuous Improvement in Clinical AI — Abridge
summaryLinesEn: By grounding prioritization in clinical demand and feedback, we can identify where a one-size-fits-all model may not capture the realities of a given specialty.
By the end of the December 2025 sprint, Abridge moved several new specialty model updates into General Availability, including Hematology-Oncology, Gastroenterology, and the full surgical suite.

One-click surveys and simple thumbs up/down signals help us capture feedback early, whether that’s an Orthopedic surgeon preferring a “more concise” HPI or an Emergency Medicine clinician requesting a more tightly structured, problem-first assessment.

sourceContent.headline: Innovation at the Speed of Trust: Continuous Improvement in Clinical AI — Abridge
sourceContent.description: Discover how Abridge builds specialty-specific clinical AI models—using multi-layered validation to ensure safe, seamless updates.
paragraphs: By grounding prioritization in clinical demand and feedback, we can identify where a one-size-fits-all model may not capture the realities of a given specialty.
By the end of the December 2025 sprint, Abridge moved several new specialty model updates into General Availability, including Hematology-Oncology, Gastroenterology, and the full surgical suite.

One-click surveys and simple thumbs up/down signals help us capture feedback early, whether that’s an Orthopedic surgeon preferring a “more concise” HPI or an Emergency Medicine clinician requesting a more tightly structured, problem-first assessment.

In December 2025, Abridge rolled out several new specialty-specific model updates, advancing from adaptable note-taking to deeply distinctive, clinician-aligned documentation tailored to highly specialized workflows. These updates are developed and rigorously evaluated to ensure measurable gains in note quality before they are released into the hands of clinicians, which is all part of Abridge’s continuous improvement process for clinical AI.

When these model updates are ready, they are shipped “quietly,” which is to say without build, configuration, or workflow disruption. Health systems are not asked to implement new versions. Clinicians are not prompted to update apps. The process is seamless, enhancing care delivery without interrupting it. Clinicians simply experience better notes, automatically.

At Abridge, our documentation models support clinicians across specialties, care settings, and systems at scale. It’s that scale that gives us the opportunity to go a million miles deep in specific specialties to make them even better.

articles.title: Now you can explore any idea in parallel without touching what's live | Lovable

summaryLinesEn: Our sales teams have been building their own tools with Lovable, from the Sales hub where we manage our sales pipeline to our demo library.

You can even ask Lovable to spin up different versions for you and keep the ones you like.

articles.title: Updating our coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy timelines
articles.descEn: We’re shortening our vulnerability disclosure window from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues.
articles.titleEn: Updating our coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy timelines
summaryLinesEn: We are now notifying the maintainers of these projects that we are providing them an additional 30 days, after which time we will publish these reports on our dashboard in line with our updated policy starting January 1, 2027.
These policies assumed that fixes moved at human speed and that independent rediscovery of the same bug was unlikely.
Maintainers of critical open-source projects can apply to OSS Scanner , a no-cost service that periodically scans their code with our strongest models and sends them findings directly.

articles.title: Use prompt caching with open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: Many generative AI applications resend the same long context on every request. Prompt caching lets open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock reuse it to reduce input cost and latency. This post shows implicit and explicit caching through the Chat Completions API and applies caching to an OpenCode coding agent session.
articles.titleEn: Use prompt caching with open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: Amazon Bedrock sends the request to the selected open-weight model and returns the response, including the cache usage fields that the following sections show you how to read.

This post presents eight best practices for writing a topic precisely enough that the guardrail blocks what you mean and passes what you don't.

articles.title: New AI training performance benchmarks for Google TPUs
articles.descEn: In the latest MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark round, Google Cloud published 10 results across seventh-generation Ironwood TPUs and NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs, spanning f…
articles.titleEn: New AI training performance benchmarks for Google TPUs
summaryLinesEn: Agentic RL on Ironwood: 640 Ironwood TPUs reached the target model’s coding benchmark target accuracy in 18.02 minutes (0.765 vs. the 0.69 goal), running code generation and learning simultaneously so training chips waited under 3% of the time.

Built on Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer architecture, these results reflect co-design across silicon, networking, and open software: Pre-training on Ironwood: 8,192 Ironwood TPUs reached the target model's benchmark target quality in 1.70 minutes, scaling up to 4,096 chips with 96% efficiency.

NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs: On Google Cloud A4X Max Instances, 256 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs for pre-training benchmark reached the target quality in 31.96 minutes, complemented by five A4X and A4X Max submissions on the agentic RL benchmark.

articles.title: CUDA at 20: How the Platform Transformed Scientific Computing
articles.descEn: Over two decades, CUDA, the platform that turned GPUs into the engine of modern science, has advanced Nobel Prize-winning research and more.
articles.titleEn: CUDA at 20: How the Platform Transformed Scientific Computing
summaryLinesEn: Today, more than 11 million developers build on CUDA across the computing stack.
At the platform’s core is this developer community whose experiments, tools and persistence expanded what accelerated computing could do.
In 2013, researchers at Illinois, the University of Pittsburgh and Vanderbilt University used CUDA-accelerated tools to help resolve the HIV capsid’s atomic structure.

articles.title: NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training and Endpoints as Vera Rubin Debuts With Leading Performance
articles.descEn: In its MLPerf benchmarks debut, with results released today, the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform delivers leading performance across training, post-training and agentic inference.
articles.titleEn: NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training and Endpoints as Vera Rubin Debuts With Leading Performance
summaryLinesEn: In its debut, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered up to 2x more performance per GPU than the highly optimized NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 system — early results that show the pace of generation-over-generation innovation.
On the DeepSeek-V3 benchmark, Vera Rubin NVL72 scaled from 256 to 1,024 GPUs with about 97% efficiency: quadrupling the GPUs cut time to train from 16 minutes to about four.

NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark and, in its first MLPerf Endpoints submission, delivered more than 10x generational gains in throughput per watt for agentic AI — measuring how much agentic work a system delivers with each watt of power.

articles.title: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics
articles.descEn: Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches.
articles.titleEn: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics
summaryLinesEn: Cooler Optics, Replaceable Light Sources Increase Resiliency Lambda’s deployment uses NVIDIA Photonics switches, each with 144 ports running at 800Gb/s.

By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics.

The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale.

articles.title: Get answers from tables with tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports tabular search, so agentic retrieval can answer questions over CSV, XLSX, and XLS files. It looks up values and runs calculations across every relevant row, then combines the results with facts from related documents to answer multi-step analytical questions.
articles.titleEn: Get answers from tables with tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: An answer built from them uses a handful of rows, so a total, a comparison, or a threshold check can be incomplete.

articles.title: Tabular foundation models on Databricks AI Runtime | Databricks Blog
articles.descEn: Tabular foundation models can make predictions on new datasets without training a task-specific model, speeding up predictive ML experiments.
articles.titleEn: Tabular foundation models on Databricks AI Runtime | Databricks Blog
summaryLinesEn: From credit risk and customer churn to demand forecasting and predictive maintenance, these use cases have traditionally required teams to develop, train and maintain models for each prediction task.
Compare tabular foundation models with existing baselines on accuracy, inference latency, GPU memory use and cost before choosing a model.
Tabular foundation models (TFMs) offer another approach: pretrained models that can make predictions on new datasets without task-specific training.

articles.title: Novo Nordisk modernizes manufacturing process documents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: Novo Nordisk's Manufacturing Technology team within the Tablet area team built a process-intelligence assistant on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using a GraphRAG architecture that pairs a knowledge graph in Amazon Neptune with hybrid search in Amazon OpenSearch Serverless to turn millions of controlled manufacturing documents into grounded, cited answers.
articles.titleEn: Novo Nordisk modernizes manufacturing process documents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: This follows recent research on clarifying ambiguous questions before retrieval and on using a knowledge graph to supply the clarification options rather than letting the model invent them.

Over the past couple of years, the consensus has shifted toward ontology-guided extraction using a predefined, domain-specific schema to guide the model, which improves accuracy and reliability for specialized corpora.
This dependency on tribal knowledge creates bottlenecks that slow down decision-making and, ultimately, impact how quickly life-saving medicines reach patients.

articles.title: Modernizing mainframe Assembler to Java using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: Legacy mainframe Assembler applications are costly to maintain and hard to staff. This post presents a multi-stage, AI-powered methodology using Amazon Bedrock, Kiro IDE, and AWS Transform to extract business rules, convert Assembler through an intermediate COBOL stage, and deploy modernized Java Spring Boot applications on AWS.
articles.titleEn: Modernizing mainframe Assembler to Java using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: Amazon Bedrock doesn’t use your prompts or model outputs to train AWS models or share them with third parties.

This post shows you a multi-stage transformation methodology using Amazon Bedrock , Kiro IDE (an AI-powered integrated development environment), and AWS Transform that can help reduce modernization time compared to manual approaches while maintaining business logic integrity through validation checkpoints.
The modernization solution helps you transform legacy mainframe Assembler applications into Java applications built for the AWS cloud through a multi-phase, AI-powered workflow.

articles.title: How MoEngage built agentic customer engagement on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: MoEngage built Merlin AI, a set of AI agents on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that let marketing and product teams draft, analyze, and adjust campaigns from a single conversation. Learn how MoEngage turned its existing APIs into MCP tools and kept each tenant's data isolated while giving agents secure access to live platform data.
articles.titleEn: How MoEngage built agentic customer engagement on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: All four share the same foundation: foundation models in Amazon Bedrock for reasoning and generation, AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, for hosting, and MCP for standardized access to data.
This capability points to a broader shift in software platforms.

For a customer engagement platform, that means a capability already exposed as an API can become a tool an agent calls, and a campaign that once moved across several tools can move through one conversation instead.

summaryLinesEn: Google Cloud leaders share what to expect in cybersecurity for 2027.
